principles: Keep DONE/REVIEW/TEST gates unchanged and fail closed.
Keep local lifecycle readiness separate from Authority and production completion.
Automate only mechanical steps that already exist today.
Avoid pre-DONE mutations that change material hash after readiness is computed.
drivers: Reduce repeated manual closure sequencing time.
Prevent false DONE-ready output after metadata or version file mutation.
Reuse existing done_closure, validate, and stale evidence machinery.
Make blocked states actionable with exact next commands.

options.name: A: Pre-DONE readiness assistant only
pros: Preserves lifecycle boundaries and avoids material hash invalidation from version changes.
Can reuse existing validate and done_closure semantics.
Keeps Authority and production claims out of local automation.
cons: Does not fully automate post-DONE version bump in this story.
Some stale evidence cases may still require a second run after committing metadata.

options.name: B: One command that prepares DONE and bumps runtime version before DONE
pros: Looks faster from a single-command operator perspective.
Could reduce one extra manual finalization step.
cons: Version file mutation changes material hash and can stale the evidence that made DONE ready.
High risk of dirty worktree blocking story_advance DONE after done_prepare says PASS.
Blurs pre-DONE readiness with post-DONE main finalization.

options.name: C: Documentation-only runbook with no command implementation
pros: No chance of changing lifecycle behavior.
cons: Does not reduce the repeated manual steps that caused the delay.
Leaves agents to keep sequencing merge, refresh, validate, and done_closure manually.

rationale: Choose A because it fixes the real workflow problem while preserving evidence correctness. It automates merge-main, stale evidence handling, validate, done_closure, clean-tree checks, and runtime-change reporting, but deliberately leaves version mutation for post-DONE local main finalization.

preMortem.scenario: done_prepare prints PASS after validate refreshes metadata and leaves the worktree dirty.
preMortem.trigger: Handler does not run a final git status check after validate or stale evidence refresh.
preMortem.consequence: story_advance DONE immediately fails or, worse, operator trusts a false ready state.
preMortem.mitigation: Always run final clean-tree check; block at cleanTree with exact files and commit guidance.

preMortem.scenario: done_prepare mutates version files before DONE and invalidates material evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Runtime-change detection is implemented as a version bump inside the pre-DONE command.
preMortem.consequence: materialHash changes after done_closure, making evidence stale and undermining the strong-evidence flow.
preMortem.mitigation: Do not accept versionBump in done_prepare; only report postDoneRuntimeVersionBumpRequired.

preMortem.scenario: Local DONE readiness is mistaken for Authority DONE or production DONE.
preMortem.trigger: Output collapses done_closure local audit, degraded-single-host fallback, Authority receipt status, and production completion into one PASS line.
preMortem.consequence: Users overclaim completion and downstream systems trust local-only evidence as remote proof.
preMortem.mitigation: Render authorityDone=false, fullAuthorityDone=false, productionDone=false unless verified Authority receipt paths explicitly say otherwise; never claim them in this command.

preMortem.scenario: Stale evidence is silently refreshed when real rerun is needed.
preMortem.trigger: Handler hides dryRun transcript and always runs refresh without showing what changed.
preMortem.consequence: Evidence may appear fresh without enough operator context.
preMortem.mitigation: Run dryRun first, surface stale transcript, reuse existing refresh only when enabled, and preserve validate/done_closure as final gates.
